description: Figure 3 presents two sets of pie charts comparing problem distribution based on correctness under w/ knowledge and w/o knowledge settings using CoT and Verify-All prompting methods. The top row displays results for the CoT method, showing three pie charts labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard.” The “easy” chart is divided into four segments: teal (40.6%), yellow (45.9%), light green (3.3%), and orange (10.1%). The “medium” chart has four segments: teal (44.6%), yellow (44.3%), light green (3.9%), and orange (7.2%). The “hard” chart is split into four segments: teal (36.2%), yellow (36.8%), light green (20.1%), and orange (7.0%). The bottom row shows results for the Verify-All method, also with three pie charts labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard.” The “easy” chart contains four segments: teal (61.5%), yellow (34.6%), light green (9.8%), and orange (1.5%). The “medium” chart has four segments: teal (65.4%), yellow (30.8%), light green (1.5%), and orange (2.3%). The “hard” chart is divided into four segments: teal (39.6%), yellow (30.6%), light green (25.1%), and orange (4.7%). A legend to the right of each set indicates the color coding: teal for N+K+, yellow for N+K–, light green for N–K+, and orange for N–K–. Each pie chart includes percentage labels within its respective slices, and the slices appear to be arranged in descending order by size within each chart.
